blocks.content:
• Vertical erosion dominates in youthful stage.
• Lateral erosion forms meanders.
• Oxbow lakes form from cut-off meanders.
• Sea level is ultimate base level.
• Dendritic drainage resembles tree branches.
Sea level is ultimate base level.

items: Distinguish between vertical erosion (youthful stage) and lateral erosion (meanders) as this distinction is commonly tested.
Remember that oxbow lakes are specifically formed from cut-off meanders.
Identify dendritic drainage pattern by its resemblance to tree branches.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Vertical erosion dominates during the youthful stage of a river.
Lateral erosion leads to the formation of river meanders.
Oxbow lakes are created from cut-off meanders.
Sea level is the ultimate base level for erosion.
Dendritic drainage pattern resembles tree branches.
